name: Red plum
lede: Red plum is a bright, warm pink-red named for the fruit, with only a thin Japanese-sourced record in our library and an identical twin under a second name.

sections.title: A fruit color with little paper trail
sections.body:
ColorHub's library carries Red plum through a Japanese source with no recorded date and no plate or block number, so when the name was coined and by whom are both undocumented here [1]. The hex value #DB5A6B is a screen approximation; no pigment or dye is named in our sources [1]. The identical color point also carries the library name [[red-plum|Dusty Cerise]], a second catalog entry for the same swatch [2].

Past that exact duplicate, the nearest distinct neighbor is [[mayflower|Mayflower]], 3.0 units away and slightly more orange; [[carmine-red|Carmine Red]] sits 4.0 units off, and [[paradise-pink|Paradise Pink]] is 4.4 units away, both brighter [2]. In LCH terms Red plum measures lightness 56, chroma 55, hue 18 degrees[2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Red plum in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, 0.03 percent, as photographed, rarer than 77 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. Where it appears, it plays an accent in every instance rather than a shadow or a mid-tone [3]. The archive is too thin here to name a leading painter, century or country with confidence [3]. As a bright, saturated red, it is also one of the colors most sensitive to a canvas's varnish and lighting, so each match is read with that caveat [3].
